examples.text: „Die Natur, in welcher ich zu handeln habe, ist nicht ein fremdes, ohne Rücksicht auf mich zu Stande gebrachtes Wesen, in welches ich nie eindringen könnte. Sie ist durch meine eignen Denkgesetze gebildet, und muß wohl mit denselben übereinstimmen; sie muß wohl mir überall durchaus durchsichtig, und erkennbar, und durchdringbar sein bis in ihr Inneres.“

glosses: Capable of being penetrated, entered, or pierced.

examples.text: On the east the high mountain-chain of Zagros, penetrable only in one or two places, forms a barrier of the most marked character, and is beyond a doubt the natural limit for which we are looking.
A Boer may know you, but it will take you some time to know him, and when a certain stage in your acquaintance is reached, you may begin to wonder whether his real nature is penetrable at all.
A capacity is cognitively penetrable in this sense if that capacity is affected by the subject's knowledge or ignorance of the domain.

glosses: Able to be permeated; absorbing or allowing the passage of fluids.

examples.text: Rainwater sinks through permeable rock to form an underground reservoir.
One hundred thirty-one small, highly permeable masonry wall specimens built of concrete blocks or of bricks were treated with cement-water paints or with other waterproofings.

glosses: Allowing the passage of persons, information, or other things, especially when such passage occurs despite hopes or expectations otherwise.
(di) corpo in grado di lasciarsi attraversare da liquidi o gas
(di) roccia capace di farsi attraversare da un fluido
